_comment: integration-cc7ab spike evidence. Redacted request/response sequence for the WORKING auth route (adp-signed request, ADR-0074 amendment). Recorded live against the marketplace `de` host using the builder's own audible-cli auth file. Every token, signature, cookie value, customer id, device serial and key below is `<redacted>`; a real capture would have full-length base64/opaque strings in their place. Not wired into any test (TDD_SKIPPED: spike — evidence only) — a real test would need a live network stub, which is out of this spike's scope.

sequence.purpose: Mint an access token from the imported refresh_token (existing Audible.fs refreshAccessToken flow — unchanged by this spike, included only for sequence completeness).
Find a library item with a companion PDF (existing GET /1.0/library shape — unchanged by this spike).

ROUTE 1 (WORKS): signed x-adp request against the companion-file endpoint, following its redirect. This is the request the ADR amendment newly allows. Matches mkb79/audible's Authenticator.sign_request shape.

signing.signatureComputation: RSA-SHA256 sign of signedString using the auth file's device_private_key (PKCS1 PEM, 'RSA PRIVATE KEY'); result base64-encoded

request.note: No Authorization/bearer header, no client-id header — signing headers alone.

firstAttempt.note: A fresh, signed redirect target — NOT the same as the static, unsigned pdf_url from step 2's library response. This is the key difference from the prior bounced attempt (integration-qqpq9), which only ever tried a bearer token and got redirected to www.amazon.de/ap/signin, or hit the raw pdf_url directly and got a CloudFront 403 AccessDenied.

followedRedirect.verdict: Real PDF body. Route 1 alone is sufficient — no cookie exchange needed.

sequence.purpose: ROUTE 2 (also confirmed to work, but NOT recommended — route 1 is simpler and was tried first per the task's ordering). refresh_token -> website cookie exchange (mkb79/audible's refresh_website_cookies / alexapy's exchangetoken pattern), then companion-file with the minted cookies.

conclusion: Route 1 (adp-signed request to /companion-file/<asin>, following its redirect) reaches a real PDF body using only the imported auth file's adp_token + device_private_key — the same two fields ADR-0074 already imports 'for signed requests' but the adapter never used until now. No login, no /auth/register, no cookie exchange required. See the ADR amendment reported in this task's Outcome.
